title: Pointed Abel maps, their divisor images, and the universal Picard family
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $C/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve [def-sc-curves, def-kun-projective] of genus $g\geq1$ [def-sc-genus], choose $P\in C(k)$, and fix a Jacobian $J$ with its representing isomorphism [def-sc-jacobian]. There is an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M_P$ on $C\times_kJ$ [def-sc-invertible-module], trivial on $\{P\}\times J$ and $C\times\{0\}$, representing the identity of the degree-zero Picard functor. For every $k$-scheme $T$, pulling back $\mathcal M_P$ identifies maps $T\to J$ with isomorphism classes of fibrewise degree-zero invertible sheaves on $C\times T$ rigidified along $P\times T$. The morphism $f_P:C\to J$ defined by the class $Q\mapsto[\mathcal O_C(Q-P)]$ is a closed immersion. For $0\leq r\leq g$, let $C^{(r)}$ denote the scheme of effective divisors of degree $r$ on $C$ (the Hilbert scheme of [thm-pc-hilb-curves]), and let
$$f_P^{(r)}:C^{(r)}\longrightarrow J,\qquad D\longmapsto[\mathcal O_C(D-rP)]$$
be the Abel morphism [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism]. Its scheme-theoretic image $W_r$ is integral of dimension $r$, and $f_P^{(r)}:C^{(r)}\to W_r$ is birational. In particular $W_g=J$, and $W_{g-1}$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $J$. Under the isomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}^{r}_{C/k}\to J$ given by tensoring with $\mathcal O_C(-rP)$, $W_r$ is precisely the scheme-theoretic image of effective divisors of degree $r$. Divisors, their degrees and $\mathcal O_C(D)$ are as in [def-sc-divisor].

source.place: Chapter III Theorems 1.6–1.7 and Lemma 1.8, pp.88–89 (normalized universal family); §2, pp.91–93, especially Proposition 2.3 (Abel embedding); §5, p.100 and Theorem 5.1(a), p.101 (birationality onto W_r); §6, paragraph before Theorem 6.6, p.105 (W_{g-1} is a divisor).

proof.text: First [lem-pc-projective-proper] makes $C$ proper, [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings] makes it integral, and [prop-pc-xk-integral], using $P$, makes it geometrically integral. Normalize the universal Picard class. The isomorphism in [def-sc-jacobian], restricted to the rigidified description in [sk-prop-picard-pic-split], identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_k(T,J)$ naturally with the isomorphism classes of degree-zero pairs $(\mathcal L,\alpha:P_T^*\mathcal L\simeq\mathcal O_T)$. That result applies to this smooth proper geometrically connected curve and supplies the universal equality $\mathcal O_T\simeq q_*\mathcal O_{C_T}$, including nonreduced and disconnected $T$. Evaluate the natural identification at $T=J$ and $\mathrm{id}_J$ to obtain $(\mathcal M_P,\alpha_P)$. Naturality says that a map $u:T\to J$ corresponds to $(1_C\times u)^*(\mathcal M_P,\alpha_P)$; hence this is the required bijection for every $T$. The fibre at $0$ is the trivial degree-zero class because the representing isomorphism is a group isomorphism, so $\mathcal M_P|_{C\times\{0\}}\simeq\mathcal O_C$. This proves both normalizations and the full universal-family assertion.

source.place: III Theorems 1.6–1.7 and proof of Lemma 1.8, pp.88–89.

proof.text: Set $H_r=C^{(r)}=\operatorname{Hilb}^r_{C/k}$. The curve is integral by [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings], and is geometrically integral by [prop-pc-xk-integral], applied with the given point $P$. Thus [thm-pc-hilb-curves] gives a smooth proper variety $H_r$ of dimension $r$, for every $r\geq0$. Tensoring with $\mathcal O_C(-rP)$ gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}^r_{C/k}\to J$ by [prop-pd-picard-degree-decomposition] and the chosen representing isomorphism [def-sc-jacobian]. Its inverse tensors with $\mathcal O_C(rP)$, so it is an isomorphism on the entire functor, not just on $k$-points. Compose the divisor-to-Picard morphism of [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism] with this isomorphism to construct $a_r=f_P^{(r)}$. It sends $D$ to $[\mathcal O_C(D-rP)]$. In comparing the Hilbert-divisor and rational-function divisor conventions, use [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-agrees-sc].

source.place: III §1, pp.86–89, and §5 opening, p.100; Stacks Tag 0B9I for the divisor Hilbert scheme.

proof.text: Identify $H_1$ with $C$ functorially, using the $T$-point definition of [def-pc-hilb-functor]. A finite locally free rank-one closed subscheme $D\subset C_T$ has $D\simeq T$: the unit $\mathcal O_T\to q_*\mathcal O_D$ is a map between rank-one modules which is an isomorphism on every residue-field fibre, hence is an isomorphism locally. Consequently $D$ is the graph of a unique $T\to C$. Conversely the graph of any $T\to C$ is a section of the proper projection $C_T\to T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. It is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion], is finite locally free of rank one over $T$, and so is an element of the Hilbert functor. These constructions are inverse and commute with pullback. The representing property of [thm-pc-hilb-curves] therefore identifies $H_1$ with $C$, and $a_1$ with the asserted morphism $f_P:Q\mapsto[\mathcal O_C(Q-P)]$.

source.place: III §2, pp.91–92: construction of the pointed Abel morphism; rank-one Hilbert-functor identification written out.

proof.text: For a divisor $D$ of degree $r$, the $k$-points of the full fibre of $a_r$ at $a_r(D)$ are the effective divisors $E$ of degree $r$ with $\mathcal O_C(E)\simeq\mathcal O_C(D)$. Indeed equality of the Abel classes cancels $-rP$ by the representing isomorphism. By [lem-sc-divisor-class-curve], this is precisely linear equivalence. Explicitly a nonzero rational-function section $s$ of $\mathcal O_C(D)$ gives $E=D+\operatorname{div}(s)$, and every such $E$ arises this way; two sections give the same divisor exactly when their ratio is an everywhere invertible function, hence a scalar by [lem-sc-global-functions]. Thus if $h^0(\mathcal O_C(D))=1$, this fibre has exactly the one $k$-point $D$. It has only that underlying point: it is of finite type over $k$, its closed points are $k$-points by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], and [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] makes closed points dense in every closed subset. The exact sequence of [lem-sfb-abel-differential-boundary] also shows that $(\mathrm da_r)_D$ is injective when $h^0(\mathcal O_C(D))=1$.

source.place: III §5, p.101 (fibres are complete linear systems), Theorem 5.1(b), pp.101–103.

proof.text: Each $a_r$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated], since $H_r$ is proper and $J$ is separated. Let $W_r$ be its scheme-theoretic image [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Since $H_r$ is integral, its topological image has irreducible closure. By [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image], $W_r$ is the reduced induced scheme on that closure; it is nonempty and irreducible, and hence integral. This argument specifies the scheme structure, including for $r=0$, rather than just the effective-divisor set.

source.place: III §5, pp.100–101 (closed subvariety image); scheme structure made explicit using Stacks Tag 056B.

proof.text: Here is the local argument at any $D$ with $h^0(\mathcal O_C(D))=1$. Put $y=a_r(D)$. Step 4 gives the singleton full fibre and an injective tangent map. The proper finite-fibre lemma [lem-trf-proper-finite-fibre-finite-near] makes $a_r$ finite after restricting to a neighbourhood of $y$. The injective tangent map gives a surjective cotangent map by [lem-sc-point-tangent-cotangent-surjective], and hence unramifiedness at $D$ by [lem-sc-rational-unramified-cotangent-criterion]; both residue fields are $k$. By [lem-trf-unramified-locus-base-change] choose an unramified open $O$ in the original $H_r$ containing $D$. Intersect the finite neighbourhood with the complement of the closed image $a_r(H_r\setminus O)$ under the original proper morphism. This does not remove $y$, since its entire fibre is $D$, and the restricted finite map is now everywhere unramified. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-unramified-one-point-closed]: the remaining hypotheses are the same singleton fibre and the identity extension $k/k$, which is purely inseparable. It gives an open neighbourhood $V$ of $y$ such that $a_r^{-1}(V)\to V$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: III Lemma 2.4, p.92, and proof of Theorem 5.1(a), p.102; local form: Stacks Tags 02UP, 0B2E, 0B2G, 04DG.

proof.text: For $r=1$, [lem-sfb-small-degree-divisor-sections] says $h^0(\mathcal O_C(Q))=1$ at every $Q\in C(k)$. Step 6 therefore supplies closed-immersion neighbourhoods of every closed point of the image of $a_1$. The complement of the image is open, since $a_1$ is proper, and the inverse image there is empty. These opens cover $J$: their complement is closed, and if nonempty it would contain a closed point, by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], contrary to their construction (closed fibre points are rational by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]). Now [lem-weil-pbc-closed-finite-etale-zariski-local] implies $a_1$ is a closed immersion. Via Step 3 this is the required closed immersion $f_P:C\hookrightarrow J$.

For each $0\leq r\leq g$, choose $D$ with $h^0(\mathcal O_C(D))=1$ by [lem-sfb-small-degree-divisor-sections]. The open $V$ in Step 6 meets $W_r$, and [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open] identifies the scheme-theoretic image of $a_r^{-1}(V)\to V$ with $W_r\cap V$. Since this restricted morphism is a closed immersion, it identifies its source with its scheme-theoretic image: on affine opens both are the quotient by the kernel of the same surjection. Thus $a_r$ identifies nonempty open subschemes of the integral schemes $H_r$ and $W_r$, proving birationality. By [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic] nonempty opens of each integral variety have its dimension, so $\dim W_r=\dim H_r=r$. For $r=0$ the chosen divisor is the zero divisor and the same argument gives the reduced point $W_0=\{0\}$; no positive-degree assertion was used.

source.place: III Lemma 5.2 and Theorem 5.1(a), pp.101–103; includes the zero-divisor endpoint.

proof.text: For $r=g$, [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-surjective] says that $H_g\to\operatorname{Pic}^g_{C/k}$ is surjective. Composing with the isomorphism of Step 2 makes $a_g$ surjective. The scheme $J$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], since it is an abelian variety [def-sc-jacobian, def-sc-abelian-variety], and integral by [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral]. By [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image] the scheme image of the reduced source $H_g$ is therefore all of $J$, not a thickening of it. Hence $W_g=J$.

source.place: III Theorem 5.1(a), p.101; Stacks divisor-to-Picard surjectivity for degree g.

proof.text: Finally $J$ is an abelian variety of dimension $g$ [def-sc-jacobian, def-sc-abelian-variety], and Step 9 shows that it is regular and integral; it is locally Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. Step 5 makes $W_{g-1}$ an integral closed subscheme of $J$; let $\xi$ be its generic point. Step 8 gives $\dim W_{g-1}=g-1$. By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains], $\dim\mathcal O_{J,\xi}$ is the supremum of the lengths of chains $W_{g-1}=Z_0\subsetneq Z_1\subsetneq\cdots$ of irreducible closed subsets of $J$. It is at least $1$: $W_{g-1}\neq J$, since their dimensions $g-1<g$ differ, and $W_{g-1}\subsetneq J$ is such a chain. It is at most $1$. Take a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $W_{g-1}$ of length $g-1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Its top member is $W_{g-1}$ itself, since otherwise appending the irreducible closed set $W_{g-1}$ would give a chain of length $g$ in $W_{g-1}$. Its members are closed in $J$. If there were a chain $W_{g-1}\subsetneq Z_1\subsetneq Z_2$ in $J$, appending $Z_1,Z_2$ would give a chain of length $g+1$ in $J$, contrary to $\dim J=g$. Hence $\dim\mathcal O_{J,\xi}=1$. Now apply [lem-per-regular-prime-divisor-local-equations] to the integral, regular, locally Noetherian scheme $J$ and the integral closed subscheme $W_{g-1}$ whose generic point has one-dimensional local ring. It shows that the ideal of $W_{g-1}$ is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], so $W_{g-1}$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $J$. In genus one this says exactly that the reduced origin $W_0$ is Cartier on the smooth curve $J$. For any $r$, the final identification with the effective-divisor image in $\operatorname{Pic}^r$ follows on schemes from Step 2: its isomorphism with $J$ takes the Abel morphism to $a_r$, and the smallest closed subscheme through which a morphism factors is carried to the smallest such closed subscheme by an isomorphism.

source.place: III §6, paragraph before Theorem 6.6, p.105; Stacks Tag 0BXH for the Cartier upgrade.
